articleTitle: 5G: An Overview on Challenges and Key Solutions
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The next generation of mobile communications, 5G, is currently being developed and expected to be commercially available by 2020. Unlike the previous generations, 5G will bring massive changes by enabling ultra-reliable communication, ultra-dense deployment, higher data rates, lower latencies and higher spectrum efficiency and energy efficiency. Nonetheless, the today's hardware structure and technologies used cannot support the requirements proposed for 5G. Therefore, new solutions and key technologies need to be investigated. This article provides an overview on the existing challenges in order to reach the requirements proposed for the next generation, and the key technologies that act as solutions to these challenges.

articleTitle: Blockchain and Consensus Algorithms in Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: this paper focuses on the performance evaluation of consensus algorithms used in a blockchain system for Internet of Things (IoT). In such systems the time necessary to achieve consensus should be small. Three most used consensus algorithms (modified proof of work, practical byzantine fault tolerance and binary consensus) are evaluated in different situations – type of motes, number of nodes participating in consensus algorithm and radio propagation model. An integrated solution is proposed to adapt an IoT node to different consensus algorithm. The simulations in Contiki IoT operating system show good performance (time to achieve consensus less than seconds)

articleTitle: Adding audio capabilities to TIAGo service robot
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Service robots are extensively used these days for industry and assisted living applications. In this work we present how the capabilities of the TIAGo robot can be extended. We show that it can handle tasks received through audio signals. Experimental results are provided to support our claims.

articleTitle: Face Detection and Recognition Based on General Purpose DNN Object Detector
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Facial recognition is a very on-demand task today. What makes a racial detection and recognition system good is its robustness to changes in illumination, rotation and tilt, position and occlusion. In this paper we present a face recognition system trained on a proprietary datatabase. Our method is based on YOLO (You Only Look Once) model, which is a general object detection system, that by modifying and testing different internal parameters we have proven it to be adequate for face recognition. The database was created especially for this project, with images featuring 10 different subjects, different orientations, and illumination conditions, totalling to 120.000 samples. The models were based on 17 variations of the architecture of Darknet-19 neural network, from which we have chosen the one with the best results.

articleTitle: Comparison of Hexagonal and Square Coils for Use in Wireless Charging of Electric Vehicle Battery
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The interest in electric vehicles is increasing day by day due to the reduction of fossil fuel resources and the environmental pollution caused by the use of these resources. Increased attention to electrical vehicles has also led the way to search for more practical and reliable methods to use them. Wireless power transfer (WPT) is also receiving attention for several applications and it is viewed as the choice of battery charging systems for near future. In this study, the coupling coefficients of different coil structures with equal winding area are compared. Taking into consideration the obtained results, a 2.2 kW WPT system to charge has been designed with square and hexagonal coil and its Finite Element Analysis (FEA) simulation has been carried out by using Maxwell Ansys. Simulation results show, hexagonal coil shape is less sensitive to misalignment conditions and is a good candidate for EV applications.

articleTitle: Implementation of Google Assistant on Rasberry Pi
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper investigates the implementation of the voice Google assistant on a Raspberry Pi microcomputer. First, the Voice Kit of Google is presented. This device can be attached to a Raspberry Pi and a voice Google assistant is obtained. The necessary steps to implement the voice Google assistant on a system that contains among the Raspberry Pi only a microphone and a speaker, instead of the Voice Kit, are presented. In this way a voice Google assistant can be made more easily and flexible. This newly created device has several working modes that are analyzed. Finally, a speech recognition system that works in Romanian language is presented and evaluated.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of a Chaos Based PRNG Targetting Secret Communication
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper describes the digital implementation of a chaos based cyptographic pseudo-random number generator using a Zynq SoC, offloading the computation to the FPGA. The implementation is based on the generalized Henon map, and it is done using fixed point 3.61 arithmetic. We will show that there is a performance improvement compared to the execution on the ARM Cortex A9 processor and that the generated random bytes are consistent with the software implementation. The generator is tested against the NIST, Dieharder and TestU01 suites.

articleTitle: VR for Education in Information and Tehnology: application for Bubble Sort
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The paper presents our work consisting of a mobile 3D application for learning the Bubble Sort sorting algorithm. To raise the interactivity and the students' interest for learning sorting algorithms we propose an application based on Virtual Reality technology and the VR headset. The application's design is based on the gamification concept supporting an easy learning process. Respecting the gamification concept, using the VR application among students, has led to a more effective learning of the Bubble Sort sorting algorithm. The bubble sort algorithm learning application, is designed in the Unity editor with C# scripts to implement the functionality.

articleTitle: Driver Drowsiness Detection Based on Eye Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Safe car driving has become a priority in everyday life. The main reason for designing a real time system which monitors the state of the driver's eyes is related to a decrease in car crashes that will benefit millions of people around the world. This work proposes a method to detect and to monitor the eyes of the driver, more precisely it analyses the eyes and check if they are closed or open. The number of frames in which eyes are closed is determined. When this number of frames is above a certain threshold, the driver will get a visual warning, on the navigation display, that points out he is drowsy.

articleTitle: Using the genetic algorithm to determine the parameters of photovoltaic cells and panels
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Heuristic methods are used more and more often to determine the parameters of photovoltaic cells and panels. The results obtained using these methods are better than the results obtained through analytical ones. The genetic algorithm is used in this paper to determine the major parameters of the photovoltaic cells and panels for a one diode model. The current voltage characteristics of the photovoltaic cells are measured under illumination in lab conditions and for the photovoltaic panels in natural sunlight conditions.

articleTitle: Indoor localization using radio beacon technology
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Indoor localization represents a hot topic nowadays due to the new emerging location-based services, which are expected to have a major impact, especially on retail sector. There are several technologies that can be used for indoor localization, such as WiFi, RFID, and Beacons. Among them, the technology based on Bluetooth Low Energy beacons, seems to be the most promising, due to the higher accuracy and low energy consumption. In this paper, some preliminary results on indoor localization based on radio beacons are presented. A localization solution based on a signal map that was built in advance is analyzed and evaluated. Conclusions about the indoor localization accuracy are presented in the end.

articleTitle: OFDM-Based Multi-Carrier Waveforms Performances in 5G
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: One of the area targeted to achieve the ambitious objectives set for the 5G is represented by new modulation and coding schemes, a new frame structure and flexible waveform referred as new radio and numerology. This paper assesses five waveforms candidates capable to handle the wide range of carrier frequency in typical 5G scenarios. The evaluated performance parameters for all these waveforms are the downlink and uplink throughput per user.

articleTitle: Dynamic programming optimization algorithm applied in test case selection
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In this paper we propose a quadratic dynamic programming algorithm applied in software testing domain, more specific in the test case selection decision making. We addressed a specific problem in software testing: running a subset of test cases from the whole set of available test cases in a limited time frame with the goal of maximizing the chances of finding potential defects. We employed both objective methods as the dynamic programming algorithm and subjective and empiric human decision as defining the selection and prioritization criteria. The proposed solution is suited for medium to large projects where in the worst-case scenarios the memory space complexity of the proposed algorithm does not exceed the order of GBytes. The proposed optimization algorithm is presented in pseudocode along with the dynamic programming recurrence formula and potential selection criteria as currently used in the industry.

articleTitle: Terrestrial Drone Creation from Rover, Robotic Arm and Raspberry Pi with Sun Tracker Function
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents the creation steps and components of a terrestrial drone. The drone is created from a rover, a robotic arm and a Raspberry Pi. The rover and robotic arm are from Lynxmotion. The rover has four motors and the robotic arm has five motors which needs to be controlled. The "brain" of the whole system is a Raspberry Pi. The rover has an "eye" too, it has a web camera to have the possibility to drive it on places where it cannot be seen by the operator. The rover has "ears"and "mouth" too be able to hear and speak. The operator can speak and it can be heard by the persons near the rover and the operator can hear the noises around the rover. The rover has a microphone built in the webcam and a separate speaker on audio interface. The rover can be controlled by an operator via Wi-Fi using a Linux machine. The computer needs to have also a speaker and a microphone connected to it, to be able to transport voice though the wireless interface, to be able to speak and hear with the rover. The rover has also sensors to follow the sun, so it has sun tracker function too. The rover it's controlled with a Python application using the arrows from the keyboard and the robotic arm is controlled with the computer's mouse. The image from the video camera from the rover is sent back on wireless interface and shown in a windows to the operator in order to be able to drive the rover.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Satellite Navigation Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper describes a comparative study of existing satellite navigation systems, highlighting their main features, as well as the advantages or disadvantages of each of them. Comparisons have also been made between the coverage of these navigation systems and the positioning accuracy offered by them.

articleTitle: Development of a Road Tax Payment Application using the Ethereum Platform
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper describes the development of a road tax payment application using the Ethereum platform. The web solution was developed using the ReactJS platform. The smart contract was developed using Remix.

articleTitle: Test bench to optimize the Powertrain in Battery-Electric and Fuel-Cell Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In the EU project SWARM a fleet of fuel cell vehicles will be developed. In this context, at Jade University a test bench was designed and practically implemented to replica a measured cyclic current of any electrical vehicles powertrain. The paper describes the practical realization and functioning of the test bench with the numerous software and hardware features. It is presented, how the measurements are received and stored in time intervals, so that the results can be evaluated at any time in Device under Test, and what happens if limits are exceeded. Results of the test bench with long-term testing of single battery cells are presented. The paper ends with the extension of the test bench to reproduce the powertrains of battery-electric and fuel-cell vehicles.

articleTitle: Adaptive Thresholding Algorithm for Noisy Electrocardiograms using Reverse Biorthogonal Mother Wavelets
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Electrocardiography aids physicians to investigate the electrical activity of the heart. Fetal signals are difficult to record and usually affected by noise, making thus a clinical diagnosis difficult. A robust and easy to implement denoising algorithm has been proposed in the present paper. The method is based on adaptive wavelet thresholding, the best mother wavelet of the reverse biorthogonal family being searched. The results are competitive and the performance has been evaluated both graphically and with objective criteria.

articleTitle: The Alphasat Experiment at Cluj-Napoca – Preliminary Results
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: As satellite communications have to keep up with the increasing demand of higher data rates, the new high throughput satellite systems have to implement several techniques to increase the system capacity. The needed bandwidth is available in the Q/V frequency band but the radio link has to be assessed and a proper channel prediction model has to be developed for a feasible end-to-end transmission. The TDP #5 module on board of the Alphasat satellite provides the means for propagation experiments in the Q/V band, while a network of ground stations deployed all over Europe evaluate the characteristics of the propagation in the Q/V band. This paper aims at presenting the Q-band beacon receiving system deployed in Cluj-Napoca and a first batch of measurement results.

articleTitle: A DNA-based chaos algorithm for an efficient image encryption application
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Nowadays, one of the important interests in the design of algorithms is their use in applications requiring real time processing. In that regard, this paper aims to present the design of an image cryptosystem based on the combination of chaotic and DNA sequences, and demonstrates its capacities and implementation through the development of a Graphical User Interface (GUI) realized under the Qt environment. To fulfill the image security and real-time requirements of today’s world, the proposed cryptosystem is symmetrical and relies on a secret key resulting from the combination of the remarkable properties of the chaos generators, with the merits of the storage space of the DNA sequences, to encrypt an image. The developed software is a didactic tool that allows the user to configure the parameters that determine the generation of the secret key, and also to encrypt and decrypt a chosen image and observe the associated statistical data. The experimental results obtained through the developed software testify first, of the simplicity of implementation of the proposed DNA-based chaos encryption scheme in real applications. It also enables the user to appreciate the performances of the algorithm in comparison to other existing algorithms in the dedicated literature, through clear and simple statistical illustrations that display a real prospect for a real-time secured image transfer over the Internet.

articleTitle: Towards Global People Detection and Tracking using Multiple Depth Sensors
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In this work a novel approach for multi depth sensor person detection and tracking from top view is presented. We propose a probabilistic framework formulating the problem of people detection in multiple overlapping depth images as an inverse problem. As a generative forward model, we employ a simple differentiable 3D person model allowing us to detect people from arbitrary viewpoints. Furthermore, we extend our probabilistic framework to allow for tracking of individuals over time. Finally, we show how to solve for the global person trajectories exploiting differentiable rendering. The preliminary evaluation shows promising qualitative results of our approach on samples of three stereo vision based depth sensors observing an indoor scene.

Author Keywords: multi camera person detection and tracking

articleTitle: Multiobjective Reinforcement Learning for Reconfigurable Adaptive Optimal Control of Manufacturing Processes
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In industrial applications of adaptive optimal control often multiple contrary objectives have to be considered. The relative importance (weights) of the objectives are often not known during the design of the control and can change with changing production conditions and requirements. In this work a novel model-free multi objective reinforcement learning approach for adaptive optimal control of manufacturing processes is proposed. The approach enables sample-efficient learning in sequences of control configurations, given by particular objective weights.

articleTitle: Evaluating hierarchical and non-hierarchical grouping for develop a smart system
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper represents a comparative study between Data Mining Techniques with the purpose to determine the architectural styles of buildings using a smart developed system and also the WEKA(Waikato Environment for Knowledge Analysis) tool. This study aims to use the clustering hierarchical algorithms (the agglomerative algorithm and the divisive algorithm) and non-hierarchical (DBSCAN - Density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise), in order to evaluate as precise as possible the system. For this evaluation, we used a system which is based on two hierarchical clustering methods.

articleTitle: From bulky analog active filters to digital filters
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In this paper we show how a bulky analog active filter, described only by its circuit diagram, can be converted to the corresponding digital filter, having the same frequency gain and phase characteristics. The state-space based approach has been implemented using Python high-level programming language. Experimental results are also presented.

articleTitle: Power Dissipation Estimation of CMOS Digital Circuits at the Gate Level in VHDL
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper proposes a static and dynamic power dissipation estimation method of CMOS digital circuits at the gate level. While static power dissipation can be easily estimated by the product of sub threshold leakage current and supply voltage, the dynamic power estimate is obtained by monitoring the switching activity in the circuit and a careful accounting of the parasitic capacitances charge/discharge. A VHDL library was developed to implement the monitoring of leakage currents and switching activity of several circuits (logic gates, encoders, multiplexers, counters) and to estimate their power dissipation. The advantage of using the library is that in early design stages assumptions can be made about the power dissipation of the designed circuit in a target technology. The downside is that the power estimation accuracy depends on the granularity of the structural description that is carried out in VHDL. To verify the estimated power, a finite state machine was implemented with standard logic gates from the 74HC series and its power dissipation was measured. The error between the measured and estimated power is approximately 20%.

articleTitle: Towards End-to-End 3D Human Avatar Shape Reconstruction from 4D Data
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: We propose a novel approach for human avatar shape reconstruction from point cloud sequences. Our approach requires no pretrained human shape model and generates a subject specific deformable shape model. Contrary to existing template-based methods, we optimize all model parameters jointly on the GPU with an off-the-shelf optimizer to deal with a large amount of free variables. Preliminary qualitative evaluation shows promising results.

articleTitle: MU-MIMO Precoding Performance Conditioned by Inter-user Angular Separation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Linear Precoding (LP) schemes are already used in Long Term Evolution (LTE) Multi-User Multiple-Input-Multiple-Output (MU-MIMO) systems. They have low complexity but do not work well in strongly correlated channels, i.e., for closely separated users. Alternatives to LP schemes, like Non-Linear Precoding (NLP) and hybrid precoding schemes were proposed in the standardization phase for 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) 5G New Radio (NR). The purpose of this paper is to analyze the performance of the existing precoding schemes in spatially correlated MU-MIMO channels, accounting for the angular separation between the users. Although NLP schemes show better results, their complexity is high and as such, hybrid schemes, which combine LP with NLP, can be used to reduce complexity without degrading too much the performance.

articleTitle: An Optimized LMS Algorithm for Bilinear Forms
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In this paper we introduce an optimized version of the least-mean-square (LMS) algorithm, which is tailored for the particular case of bilinear forms. In this context, the bilinear term is defined with respect to the impulse responses of a spatiotemporal model resembling a multiple-input/single-output system. Moreover, a comparison with the simplified version of the Kalman filter developed for bilinear forms is provided. Simulation results show the good performance of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Development of a ZettaJS driver for the ESP8266 IoT hardware
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper describes the development of a ZettaJS driver for the ESP 8266 IoT hardware device. An architecture is proposed within the framework of ZettaJS and then the implementation is described.

articleTitle: A Modified 3EED Spectrum Sensing Algorithm Using an Adaptive Decision Threshold
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Cognitive Radio (CR) systems require an efficient Spectrum Sensing (SS) technique to implement their opportunistic medium access. Energy Detection (ED) is one of the most used SS techniques. Recently, a modified ED algorithm was proposed, which investigates two additional neighboring sensing slots, besides the current one, i.e., three-Event Energy Detection 3EED. However, the previously proposed 3EED algorithm uses a fixed decision threshold, which is set for a target false-alarm probability. In this paper, we propose a novel Adaptive threshold 3EED (A3EED) algorithm that minimizes the decision error probability for given Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) and Primary User (PU) signal's average duty cycle values. Comparing the decision performance of these algorithms, for low SNR values, we prove a decision SNR gain of more than 1 dB of A3EED over the Adaptive Classical ED (ACED).

articleTitle: Simulating the Dynamic Assignment of IPv4 Addresses in an AAA-RADIUS Solution Based on LDAP and Legacy Authentication Protocols
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The simulation of static and dynamic assignment of Internet Protocol version 4 and version 6 addresses within an Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service solution, is presented in this paper. The user Authentication, Authorization and Accounting analysis is achieved using the Lightweight Directory Access Protocol, which queries the Universal State Server records. The user passwords are hashed using legacy and modern hash function families, and the Microsoft Challenge-Handshake Authentication Protocol version 1 and version 2, the Challenge-Handshake Authentication Protocol and the Password Authentication Protocol, are used to authenticate the hosts requesting access to the network. The Triple-A Language is used to develop the software program called PolicyFlow, while the solution is simulated using the 8950 AAA software from Nokia.

articleTitle: Using ICT support for STEM education in disadvantaged youth learning
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: Internet; cameras; object detection; wavelet transforms; satellite navigation; cryptography; automotive electronics; computer aided instruction; neural nets; least mean squares methods.

articleTitle: A New Hybrid Ćuk Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: A new hybrid Ćuk converter with wide step-up and step-down conversion ratio and reverse output voltage polarity relative to the input voltage is presented in this paper. Compared to the classical Ćuk converter, in step-up mode, the novel converter exhibits a wider range of the voltage conversion ratio with the same duty cycle. The DC equations are derived, the static characteristics are depicted, then stresses of devices are evaluated. The converter is simulated and experimentally tested in order to confirm the feasibility of the proposed hybrid Ćuk converter.

articleTitle: OSPA Metric for Radar Extended Object Tracker
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Past publications on multiple target tracking metrics usually considered the targets observed as being one-point source objects. This paper proposes a new method for applying the well-established Optimal Subpattern Assignment metric on automotive radar tracker algorithms, which considers for every tracked object a cluster of points in the state space, i.e. a set of several characteristic points. The method addresses the localization errors that appear during more complex, yet common driving maneuvers with multiple targets that are parking, crossing or overtaking. For three- point (closest, left-most and right-most point) extended object tracker, it is shown both in analytical and experimental way, that applying the proposed method reveals weaknesses of last generation automotive radar tracking algorithms and contributes accordingly to achieve the next level of driving automation and to increase safety on roads.

articleTitle: Touchless Fingerprint Capturing from RGB-D Images in Mobile Devices
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Touchless finger capturing for the biometric finger-print verification process in mobile devices with depth sensor is explored in this paper. Fingerprint capturing is the result of a sequence of steps, where RGB image and depth info mutually interrelated to increase the capabilities of the camera system. Hand detection and localization is initiated in the depth domain. The lower resolution depth image is used for an initial segmentation step, to identify a hand in the scene. The segmentation step with objectives finger - finger tip localization is completed using the RGB image with priors collected from depth. Fingerprint images are extracted from the image by analyzing the contour of the segmented hand palm.

articleTitle: Developing hybrid mobile applications for learning
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: During the last years, the worldwide education has been challenged and innovated by the online and blended learning approaches, and the openness towards Social Media (SM), Open Educational Resources (OERs) and Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs). Also, new opportunities are implied by the rapid diffusion of mobile technologies, mobile learning becoming a driver both in traditional and continuing education. The Politehnica University of Timisoara, Romania is one of the pioneering higher education institution in the country, adopting an open education strategy, with an important increase of the quality of education. The changing engine is represented by the eLearning Centre, which implemented the Virtual Campus (VC) platform for supporting the academic programs, and also the UniCampus MOOC platform. The main aim of this article is to present the design, implementation and evaluation of the two hybrid mobile applications for the Virtual Campus and UniCampus platforms, available for the Android and iOS operating systems, which provide flexible tools for a mobile learning approach in the university.

articleTitle: Bag of Features vs Deep Neural Networks for Face Recognition
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper proposes a comparative study of Bag of Features (BoF) and Deep Neural Networks (DNN) approaches for the problem of face recognition. For the latter approach we consider three pre-trained models, namely AlexNet, ResNet50 and GoogleNet provided through Caffe Model Zoo and use them as feature extractors. Although these models were trained on different datasets, e.g., ImageNet, bottom-most layers act like universal feature extractors thus it is possible to be employed for different classification tasks. In order to adapt the models to various face datasets requirements we performed modifications to the input data as well as to the output layer of the pre-trained models by replacing it with a multiclass SVM classifier.

articleTitle: Extension of a Glycaemic Control Medical Application with New Functions and Ergonomic User Interface Elements
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The human body is composed of numerous highly complex metabolic processes. Abnormal variation of the blood glucose concentration is a common complication in the intensive care units. This paper presents a model-based method of glycaemic control and a medical application implementing the glycaemic control protocol. The principal cases were to extend the functionality of the application in order to automatically create multiple episodes for a patient already in the database of the application and an accessibly view for previous treatments calculation. These functions are very helpful and convenient because allow to the clinicians to have new measurements and a treatment calculation without entering the data of the patient again in the system. The visualization of previous treatments can be efficiently used to define optimized dosing for the subsequent treatment period. The paper concludes with the results of the extension of the medical application.

articleTitle: A Character Prediction Approach in a Security Context using a Recurrent Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Nowadays, cybersecurity focuses on detecting intrusions and anomalies with the aid of automated methods, exploratory visual analysis systems or real-time monitoring with dynamic visual representations. Current research in cybersecurity is not yet at the point where analysts can rely on systems for assuring security. Being in a Data Era, the amount of gathered data can play opposite roles: on one side, to serve the security of an organization, but on the other, to pose security threats. Our paper aims to present a technical implementation of a recurrent neural network that predicts characters in a security context. The end goal of the proposition is to create an application for adding security to a web server by predicting log entries before an actual attack. If such a server would get a certain entry pattern, it will predict a new log before an actual attack. Results demonstrate that character prediction can be achieved with 40% accuracy.

articleTitle: Wavelets Based Filter Banks for Real Time Spectrum Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Real time spectrum analysis is realized using a filterbank whose elements need special design. We propose the wavelets based and the wavelets packets based filter banks for the implementation of a digital real time spectrum analyzer and we show the advantages of our proposition by simulation examples.

articleTitle: EGNOS Performance Improvements Using Monitoring Stations in Romania
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper describes the simulations of EGNOS performances improvements when using Ranging & Integrity Monitoring Stations (RIMS) sites in Romania, namely in Timisoara, Cluj-Napoca, Iasi and Bucharest. A reference scenario is created for the last EGNOS release, using the Service Volume Simulator SBASSimulator V1. Coverage extension is studied for different scenarios, starting from single RIMS and continuing with multiple RIMS sites scenarios. The best locations and scenarios for improving the theoretical coverage at the border area of the EGNOS service are discussed.

articleTitle: A General Approach for Deriving the Sliding Mode State-Space Equation in Second Order CCM Operated DC-DC Converters
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: A general method for deriving the sliding mode state-space equation for second order continuous conduction mode (CCM) DC-DC converters starting from the classical state space description is proposed. Opposed to most of the results in the literature that refer mainly to the classical buck, boost and buck-boost converters, the new method can be applied to any DC-DC converter. To prove this, a first order sliding mode controller for an unconventional step-down second order coupled inductor (SDSOCI) converter is designed and validated.

articleTitle: Analysis of a PM Generator with Inset Magnets
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper deals with the analyses of a three-phase synchronous generator with an inset neodymium-iron-boron permanent magnet rotor. This rotor structure produces an inverse saliency effect meaning the quadrature-axis reactance is greater than the direct-axis reactance. As a result of this effect, the generator produces reluctance-torque, improves mechanical robustness and field weakening capabilities. The paper presents some characteristics computed with Finite Element Method (FEM) and highlights some aspects of its performances: air-gap flux density distribution, cogging torque, reluctance torque, electromagnetic torque.

articleTitle: Simulating the Dynamic Assignment of IPv4 Addresses in an AAA-RADIUS Solution Based on LDAP and EAP
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The Authentication, Authorization and Accounting solution presented in this paper uses Lightweight Directory Access Protocol to query the entries of the Universal State Server, and supports the dynamic assignment of Internet Protocol version 4 information for the hosts authenticated with the Extensible Authentication Protocol. The used authentication methods are Tunneled Transport Layer Security and Transport Layer Security. The 8950 AAA program from Nokia is used to develop the PolicyFlows written in Triple-A Language, and to simulate the scenarios regarding the Extensible Authentication Protocol.

articleTitle: A solution for integrating the Vector CANCase XL with the Teradyne Test Station ICT
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents the functional technical approach and test results related to an integration between the Vector CAN Case XL (CCXL) module and the Teradyne In Circuit Tester (ICT). The proposed application is the achievement of a collaboration between two industrial partners: Continental Automotive Romania (Timişoara Plant) and Alfa Test S.R.L. The need for such an integration has originated in the context of permanent focus on innovative production solutions. Since for Continental Timişoara, Vector tools have become a traditional investigation means in the research and development process, an emerging requirement was the transfer of this technology towards the production flow. The Teradyne Test Station has been selected as the ICT which should host and use the CCXL in the functional test procedures applied to a dashboard PCB. The resulting software application is a prototype. According to the author's knowledge, there is no other similar integration which is used for production purposes. Some of the capabilities offered by this solution include: communication protocol administration between the ICT software interface and the CCXL, automated formatting of CAN messages, arithmetic conversions, CAN frames segmentation, selection of useful information embedded in exchanged frames or the combination of ICT based measurements interposed between CAN dialogs. The proposed software architecture has been validated by a series of experimental results performed on different product versions. As a reference, the First Pass Yield (FPY) parameter demonstrates that the proposed approach is viable and can be successfully used to fulfill its purpose.

articleTitle: Stand for the functional testing automation of the electronic modules
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper defines the basic concept of a stand for the automated testing of electronic modules. It is presented the development of a software application which performs the automated testing of the electronic modules using the graphic programming environment LabVIEW. The automated testing is done by establishing the GPIB communication between the measuring devices and the application developed in LabVIEW, whose input is a script file.

articleTitle: Absorber Lined Shielded Enclosure Chamber Validation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The Radiated emissions measurement is one of the tests covered by Electromagnetic testing in Automotive Industry. CISPR 25 Standard, annex J, presents the method agreed for Absorber Lined Shielded Enclosure (ALSE) Chamber Validation. In this paper a method for chamber validation is presented and validated. Because too many points were outside the tolerance limit, troubleshooting techniques were used at lower frequencies. Finally, the results are compared with results obtained from chambers from other locations.

articleTitle: Forgery detection based on reverberation time estimation in multiple bands
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In this paper we propose a system that detects an audio intrusion by analyzing the temporal evolution of an important acoustic parameter, i.e. the reverberation time (RT). Considering the forensic context of our application, we chose a blind method for estimating the reverberation time, and we propose a multiband approach for the RT's estimation. Furthermore, we introduce a succession of post-processing operations of the RT estimates in order to facilitate the detection of intrusions.

articleTitle: Towards Document Flow Discovery in e-Government Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Information and Communication Technologies are used in e-Government systems to enhance capabilities related to process, information and knowledge management. Such e-Government Systems facilitate access to services in relation to participation principles. The focus of the paper is the analysis of existing technologies related process in relation to e-government systems. The proposed approach focuses on the discovery and extraction of document flows. An automated process mining generic architecture for document flow discovery in a human-intensive environment is proposed. A case study is discussed, and the results are analyzed in relation to the main benefits.

articleTitle: Context-Based Routing Algorithm for SIP-Based Infotainment in a Smart Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Taking into consideration the amount of time spent in vehicles, in smart cities there is nowadays an interest in designing the Edge/Fog/cloud based networks in order to better serve social connectivity. This paper describes a context-based routing algorithm and its application in SIP-based infotainment. The testbed consists of a virtualized sipXcom switching system migrated into a private cloud orchestrated by OpenStack. SIP terminals placed in a smart vehicle and running Android/ Windows and Ubuntu were connected to the IP-based exchanges (both inside and outside the cloud). Regarding the capture and analysis of the SIP flows, no malfunction was detected for the system installed in the cloud (i.e. INVITE and REGISTER messages were captured properly). A lack of some SIP requests was detected for the system installed outside the cloud though, but the work to determine the reasons is under progress.

articleTitle: A Proposed Solution for Analyzing the Behavior of a WSN using a Secured Neural Network Approach
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Data collection is one of the main processes in Wireless Sensor Networks. Due to the limited capabilities of sensors and to the increased rate of attacks on these systems, researchers started to propose architectures and deploy solutions that use encryption for increasing the security level. Moreover, neural networks can play a critical role in detecting abnormal activity in the network with the end goal of minimizing the effect of attacks and fixing the issues that are causing the unwanted behavior. This paper proposes an architecture for a complete and complex secured analytical tool for studying the behavior of wireless sensors with the aid of a neural network. Security is employed through the use of a homomorphic encryption scheme that is deployed at a central point where data is aggregated from all sensors in the network through a data collection mechanism that may differ depending on the target environment. More details on the proposition will be revealed in Section III.

articleTitle: The Evaluation of the Effect of NLOS Multipath Propagation in Case of GNSS Receivers
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The precision of vehicles localization using Global Navigation Satellite Systems is affected by the multipath propagation effects, especially when the Line of Sight towards the satellites is obstructed. We evaluate the effect of Non Line of Sight multipath propagation by comparing the Cramer Rao bounds of the range estimators with and without multipath propagation.

articleTitle: Directional Measurement of HF Spectrum Occupancy
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Results concerning spectrum occupancy in HF range as function of the direction of signals arrival are reported. In addition to time and frequency, the influence of the spatial dependence on spectrum occupancy is analyzed. Spectrum occupancy is computed using an energy detection criterion. Parallel measurements of HF signals have been made using software defined radio equipment, a reference omnidirectional broadband antenna and two type of HF directional antennas. Measurements results prove that directional antenna can bring additional gain in terms of spectrum occupancy data and can offer more free frequency bands for an opportunistic transmission in an emergency communications system.

articleTitle: A Diversified Denoising System for Biomedical Images
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an image denoising system which reduce the speckle noise in medical images, while preserving the image features. The proposed denoising methods are based on wavelets functions. We have chosen denoising methods based on the Dual Tree Complex Wavelet Transform (DTCWT) and three variants of the bishrink filter. More, we propose an original denoising method that takes into account the textural and structural properties of the analyzed images.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Output Current of a Simple Switcher Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The goal of this paper is to analyze the performance of the enhanced current output of a Simple Switcher, while preserving the efficiency and the advantage of low count components. The analysis is merged with in depth simulations and comparisons for the output ripple and the dissipated power for the key elements. Specific benefits for the proposed topology are outlined.

articleTitle: Performance Queues for Fault Tolerant Sessions
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents the usefulness of queues in providing fault tolerance for real-time transmissions. Network environments gain more and more hosts every minute and because of this issue the productivity and dependability of interconnected environments have become new research topics for ensuring guaranteed end to end communications. Services which need quality of service are real-time sessions that are implemented in applications with the use of the OSI model specifications. Our work focuses mostly on the key technology features that glue together the dependencies of the last 3 layers of the OSI model with the 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> transport OSI layer and the adjacent transparent technology of the network, data-link and physical OSI model layers. In the present time and current scientific advancements communication sessions are able to function but they lack fault tolerance abilities which are very useful in routing with high workload and transmission environment stressed conditions. For this we have created a synchronization algorithm that shapes traffic via queuing methods in order to reliably reroute data traffic, the goal of the initial traffic shaping being to apply in-time adjacent router selection for real-time persistent fault tolerant sessions.

articleTitle: Interactive Adaptation Algorithm for Neurorehabilitation of Sensorimotor Function
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The treatment for motor disability's post-stroke involves repetitive training of affected limb to promote learning. Optimally designed sensor based solutions can complement the conventional approach of neuro-rehabilitation with a therapist. In this paper, we present a novel algorithm based on patient's task performance. The proposed algorithm uses “enhanced Bi-directional adaptability” with slacking factor to ensure active participation of patients. This allows the system to adapt to the requirements of participants without pre-existing knowledge of patient's disability. This not only makes it compatible to a wider range of a patient but also reduces the time required for the adaptation. The simulated results for patients with various disability levels potentially demonstrate that the system can adapt to different levels of disability.

articleTitle: Smart traffic sign detection on autonomous car
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The development and improvement of technology has enabled the use of more and more processing systems and power in nowadays cars. “Ubiquitous computing” has given the possibility of creating smarter, faster, low-power and smaller computing systems which can be integrated in automotive ECUs. Thus, cars can perform more complex operations by including ECUs with multiple cores, which can now provide multiple active safety features like real-time traffic sign detection using powerful cameras, obstacle detection using radar systems and more often highly automated cars.

articleTitle: Images’ Principal Component Analysis using Hyperanalytic Wavelet Packets
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper demonstrates the images dimensionality reduction by using a new algorithm of Principal Component Analysis based on Hyperanalytic Wavelet Packets. A new interpretation of the concept of Principal Component in case of images is proposed, taking advantage of the concrete character of directionality in this case.

articleTitle: A Comparison Between Single-Phase and Two-Phase Hybrid Boost-L Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The hybrid Boost-L converter is suitable for practical applications that require a step-up converter with wide conversion ratios. The filter stress is higher compared with the traditional Boost converter. The filter effort is reduced when using a multiphase configuration and interleaved switching. The two-phase converter is analyzed, simulated and the results are presented in this paper. Also a comparison with the single-phase Boost converter is made.

articleTitle: Effect of mixed-phase copper oxide on photovoltaic performance of p-type dye-sensitized solar cells
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The mixed-phase copper oxide with different morphologies has been successfully synthesized via a facile one-step hydrothermal method using copper (I) chloride and sodium hydroxide. The p-type dye-sensitized solar cell (DSSC) based on mixed-phase copper oxide photocathode exhibits 128 mV of open-circuit voltage (V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OC</sub>), 0.197 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of short-circuit photocurrent (J<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SC</sub>) and 0.43 of fill factor. For the enhancement of p-type dye-sensitized solar cell performance, the new morphologies of mixed-phase copper oxide should be investigated in future works.

articleTitle: Automatic testing of automotive electronic modules for cranking conditions
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: An automatic solution for implementing the testing of automotive electronic modules for cranking conditions is presented. The solution is based on an arbitrary power generator able to be programmed to repeatedly output a pulse of required shape. It is described the development of a software application which performs the automated testing using the graphic programming environment LabVIEW. The communication between sourcing and sensing devices is done through GPIB interface using SCPI commands. For validation a self test procedure was defined for cranking pulse.

articleTitle: A Comparison of Image Resizing Performance for Ubiquitous Software Platforms
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The image processing related to compression techniques represent an important topic for many research fields; the interest from various research teams stretching beyond the traditional image editing applications and entering areas such as image preprocessing for file upload over networks, image size optimization in relation to Internet bandwidth usage and so on. The present paper will try to make a contribution to some of these subjects, by providing an image resizing performance and approach comparison between three software platforms used on a large scale: Java,.NET/C # and In-Browser JavaScript.

articleTitle: Generating a Totally Focused Colour Image from Recordings of a Plenoptic Camera
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents a method to calculate a totally focussed colour image from recordings of a plenoptic camera. The three colour channels have to be extracted from the raw image. The virtual depth is estimated analyzing the disparities of image points in different microlens images which correspond to the same object point. With the such created depth map, the image points are chosen from the microlens image with correct focus to create the totally focused colour image.

articleTitle: Acquisition Modeling for Optimal Indoor Panoramic Imagery
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Given the high applicability of panoramic imagery in scene modeling, the current work addresses the process of optimal acquisition of panoramic segments. While common research contributions mainly approach a number-based optimization (number of slits optimally required to achieve a 180 × 360 ° coverage), the current solution proposes a scene-placement optimization for the panoramic equipment in an indoor capturing scenario, based on floor-plan description. The coverage area of the camera can be estimated based on the camera model and several positions can be tested to identify the best placement configuration. Given an optimal positioning in the scene, a computational implementation has been also considered to estimate the number of segments required to cover an area close to a 180 × 360 ° field-of view.

articleTitle: Capacitive Touch Sensor Used In Visually Impaired Aid Equipments
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents a capacitive touch sensor used in a visually impaired aid equipment that can be easily put into practice using a microcontroller and a few peripheral components. The hardware solution is presented as well as the software and mechanical implementations. The sensor's working principle is simple and relays on measuring the delay introduced by an extra capacitance in a RC network discharge curve. Additionally, relevant physical features of the sensor are presented together with experimental measurements characteristic curves. The sensor will be used to activate the audio feedback in a device used to guide visually impaired individuals in the surrounding background using ultrasonic distance measurements.

articleTitle: Regularized Recursive Least-Squares Algorithms for the Identification of Bilinear Forms
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The system identification problem is more challenging when the parameter space becomes large. This paper addresses the identification of bilinear systems based on the regularized recursive least-squares algorithm. Here, the bilinear term is defined with respect to the impulse responses of a spatiotemporal model. In order to improve the robustness of the algorithm in noisy environments, a variable-regularized version is also developed, where the regularization parameters are adjusted using an estimation of the signal-to-noise ratio. Simulation results outline the appealing features of these algorithms.

articleTitle: Wavelet Shrinkage of Magnetocardiograms Using the Median Absolute Deviation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Magnetocardiograms recorded in unshielded environments avoid the necessity of especially designed chambers, but are more sensitive to external interferences. Reliable denoising techniques have to be developed, which should not distort the clinical measurements. In the present paper, two filtering algorithms based on wavelet shrinkage, using intrinsic properties of the signal, have been developed and compared. The algorithm is fast computing and displays good results, enabling further improvements of the magnetocardiogram technique.

articleTitle: Retrieving Health and Environmental Data using Secure IoT Cloud platform
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Nowadays, sensors and actuators are getting noticeable in our lives since the rising focus towards body wearable sensors has become visible. Various gadgets have multiple customized applications for several purposes such as healthcare, well-being and wellness. Internet of Things (IoT) brings major changes in the way we live and within our daily routine by improving the connections between people and gadgets, providing the ability to remotely interface different objects with smart devices. Within this paper, we present the ESTABLISH project and its role, to make a safe environment that will improve the quality of life.

articleTitle: Performances of a metamaterial based on semiconductors for solar cell applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Using of semiconductors in the metamaterials for the solar cells in the place of metal avoids energy losses by conversion energy into heat. By choosing proper combinations of materials and an oriented geometry, the efficiency of the solar energy conversion can be increased with about 20 %. The semiconductor active layer is part of a metamaterials structure, with components having dimensions comparable with the semi-wavelength. The radiation domain of near infrared NIR to ultraviolet UV was considered for material testing (290...1400 nm wavelength) and the simulations were performed with HFSS 13.0. A controlled improvement of metamaterial absorbance occurs by material parameters modification, when the effective permittivity is tuned in an interval varying with more than 12 % in respect with the values reported in literature. A particular metamaterial structure was proposed (of neural type) in order to obtain these performances.

articleTitle: On the Reduced Complexity FFT Acquisition for Galileo E1 Signal
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The purpose of the paper is to present the state of the art of acquisition algorithms for GNSS signals, particularly Galileo E1, and to propose a novel, resource saving method, employing circular correlation. The results are compared against the performances of the traditional method of linear correlation and the benefits are highlited.

articleTitle: Investigation of Wave Propagation in a Plasma Antenna using 3D FDTD
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The advancement of computer technology has led numerical methods to obtain a widespread usage. One of the most frequently used numerical methods in recent years is finite difference time domain method (FDTD). The behaviour of electromagnetic waves at the boundaries of the problem space has been studied by using perfectly matched layer (PML) type boundary conditions in FDTD. On the other hand, the majority of the substances in the universe are plasma. Plasma is a well known reconfigurable medium with different dielectric and conductive properties. Operating frequency of a plasma antenna is investigated in this paper. The field distributions around the plasma antenna have been evaluated using three dimensional FDTD. It has been shown that the plasma antenna can operate with characteristics similar to a wire antenna. C/C++ and MATLAB programming environments are used for simulations.

articleTitle: Stripline Measurements in Automotive EMC: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The radiated immunity (RI) measurement is one of the tests that are necessary to validate an electronic product so that it can enter mass production. This paper is a practical approach in which a measurement setup and a calibration method for a stripline, based on the ISO 11452-5 standard, are presented. The test setup relies on measured data on different competing stripline scenarios, of which the best suited has been chosen. Our focus has been on the possible causes for variations in the uniformity of the electric field strength generated between the two plates of the stripline in order to improve the test design. Measurements reported here have been performed with two types of equipment: the one used in testing and a network analyzer.

articleTitle: Improving Regional Radio Network through Design, Simulation and Implementation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: It was analyzed the signal propagation between points which are not in direct visibility, in some areas that don't have yet access to wireless networks; the data resulted by measurements are furnished to a simulator which made the predictions for improvement of radio networks in white zones. Finally, are presented the results after the implementation of those proposals.

articleTitle: VIPERA 1.0 - A Versatile Imaging Platform for Education, Research and Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: We designed and implemented a versatile imaging platform which can be used for education, research and various applications. We used off-the-shelf components for the implementation and coded the C/C++ program required for the operation of the platform. Additional software components can be modified or added according to future needs. The imaging platform is composed of a high-speed color digital camera in Bayer format, a frame grabber and a host computer. Additionally, by using a rotating filter wheel we can use the platform for multispectral image acquisition. We created a setup with color checkers and controlled illumination for the deployment of the imaging platform in various application scenarios. We show some experimental results and draw conclusions.

articleTitle: IEEE 1451 compliant magnetic rotary transducer with energy feedback channel
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Industrial process control implies sometime the necessity to remotely operate devices placed in harsh or toxic environments, getting information from sensors powered up by batteries placed in the same environment. Thus appears the issue to periodically charge these power elements by physical removal. Hereby is developed and tested a magnetic rotary transducer which can provide energy feedback represented by periodic rectangular pulses of high voltage used to charge batteries and prolong the discharging cycle. The proposed architecture represents an IEEE 1451 compliant smart transducer communicating via industrial Ethernet.

articleTitle: Accuracy of Synchrophasor Estimation Returned by a Frequency-Domain Linear Least-Squares Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In this paper the accuracy of the synchrophasor estimator returned by the enhanced frequency-domain linear least-squares (e-FLLS) algorithm recently proposed in the scientific literature is investigated. Harmonically distorted or modulated electrical signals at off-nominal frequency are considered either in the presence or absence of additive wide- band noise. The e-FLLS algorithm is based on the rectangular window and it estimates the phasor amplitude and phase using three Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) samples. It effectively reduces the detrimental contributions of both the fundamental image component and wide-band noise on the estimated parameters. The accuracies of the e-FLLS algorithm and the corrected Interpolated DFT (IpDFTc) algorithm are then compared to each other through computer simulations in different operating conditions. As accuracy parameter the Total Vector Error (TVE) is used.

articleTitle: An overview of intelligent surveillance systems development
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In the efforts to fight against crime, city halls and governments install video surveillance system that works 24h/day like thousands of eyes in airports, ports, major roadways, government buildings and important facilities. However, such kinds of surveillance systems were strongly depended on hardware architecture and budget for installation. In this condition intelligent surveillance system (ISS) has growing attention due to the increasing demand on security and safety in areas with limited human intervention.

articleTitle: Romania Monitoring Station Network to Support EGNOS Services in Eastern Europe
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Due to its geographical location, Romania is an ideal candidate for system performance monitoring at the border of EGNOS service area. Service volume simulations were made to assess the theoretical extension of coverage of EGNOS over the Romanian territory and beyond using potential future reference station locations in Romania with whom the Politehnica University of Timisoara has agreements in place. Three monitoring stations were deployed at technical universities from Timisoara, Cluj-Napoca and Iasi with the purpose of setting up an automatic reporting of EGNOS performances over Romania.
